title: The Dissonance of the Stradivarius
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Detective Takagi, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. Episode 386 (middle of this 3-episode arc) has no subtitle file locally -- only 0385 and 0387 were read, so the mid-arc investigation scenes (e.g. exactly how Emi's stair fall two years ago was first investigated) are missing; anything from that gap is flagged 'ambiguous_cause' below rather than invented. The old cases/ file correctly identified Kyosuke Haga as the culprit, but drastically undercounted the scope of the case: it listed only 2 victims (Genzaburo, Ayane) and left the motive as 'unspecified', when the transcript reveals this is really a 4-death-plus-backstory revenge spree spanning 30 years (Danjirou Haga's death in a staged burglary cover-up 30 years ago; Chinami's death from nursing strain; Emi's stair fall 2 years ago; Furuto's veranda fall last year; Genzaburo burned this year; Ayane lured to fall this year) driven by Kyosuke discovering that his uncle Chouichirou and three others staged the cover-up that killed his father. The old file also missed the central deduction clue entirely (only Kyosuke, of the four gathered suspects, encouraged Kogoro to touch the Stradivarius again -- the actual proof of guilt) and mislabeled the murder weapon object. Furuto's status as an actual named co-conspirator in the 30-year cover-up is never explicitly confirmed on screen (only Chouichirou, Genzaburou, and Ayane are directly named staging the fake burglary, with Emi separately said to have 'colluded in the lie'); Kyosuke kills him anyway as part of a symbolic musical-scale sequence, which this file flags as motive_type ambiguity rather than asserting Furuto was a proven conspirator. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The door lock plate is bent only at the top (knob), not the bottom (bolt) -- a genuinely forced-open lock warps both, proving the door was never actually locked when it was broken down.

A stray violin bridge and a broken baton fragment turned up near Ayane's body, but both the real Stradivarius and its replica still had their bridges intact -- proving a third, rigged decoy violin was used to lure her.

Of the four gathered suspects, only Kyosuke urged Kogoro to touch the Stradivarius again; Hasuki, Choichiro, and Tsumagari all refused -- the tell that Kyosuke needed his fingerprints re-obscured because he was the one who switched the violin.
